figures.name: Figure-1.png
figures.caption: The output of the HeNe laser was expanded and directed onto the SLM to create seven parallel beams with controllable phase values. These beams were brought to a focus with a lens, and the intensity profile was measured by camera A (before the focal plane) and camera B (at the focal plane).

figures.name: Figure-2.png
figures.caption: (a) Schematic depicting the indices of all simulated fibres and the colour mapping for the phase values used in this work, and the associated experimental images recorded on camera A and camera B. (b) Examples of randomly chosen phase values and their corresponding camera A and camera B images, including the all-zero phase case.

figures.name: Figure-3.png
figures.caption: Prediction accuracy for camera A and camera B, and relative importance of camera pixels in making phase predictions calculated using gradient analysis.

figures.name: Figure-4.png
figures.caption: Flowchart of the application of deep learning for real-time bespoke beam shaping, and examples of random phase values and the progression to the final petal beam shape.

figures.name: Figure-5.png
figures.caption: Real time concept flowchart for bespoke beam shaping with additional random phase noise, examples of real-time generation of the petal profile, and power-in-the-bucket comparison.

figures.name: Figure-6.png
figures.caption: Experimental demonstration of two neural networks for determining whether a given intensity pattern is physically possible, including rotations of 0?, 30? and 60? and statistical analysis over 900 examples.
